GOT QUESTIONS?

Personal Coverage FAQ

Clear, honest answers about umbrella liability, luxury valuables, and estate protection.

Standard homeowners and auto insurance policies have maximum liability limits (typically $300k to $500k). If you are found liable for a major accident or lawsuit exceeding those limits, your personal savings, home equity, and future wages could be seized. An Umbrella policy kicks in where your underlying limits stop, providing an extra $1M to $5M+ in protection.
Standard home policies cap luxury item payouts (often around $1,500 to $2,500). Through scheduled personal property floaters, each valuable item is appraised and insured for its full agreed replacement value with zero deductible and coverage for accidental loss or breakage worldwide.
Personal Cyber protection covers expenses related to cyber extortion (ransomware), identity theft restoration, fraudulent online wire transfers, cyberbullying legal defense, and data recovery for home computer systems.
Yes! Our Personal Umbrella and Scheduled Property endorsements provide 24/7 worldwide coverage, protecting you against legal liability, lost valuables, or emergency incidents anywhere across the globe.
Personal Umbrella insurance is exceptionally cost-effective. A $1,000,000 umbrella policy typically costs between $150 and $300 per year, making it one of the most affordable ways to protect your overall financial future.
